rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading the opening letters as alphabet names says the Quran is composed of the same elements as Arabic speech, though its challengers cannot produce its like; this is the strongest of three views.
rows.anchor: هذا القرآن منتظم من جنس ما تنظمون منه كلامكم ولكن عجزتم عنه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: On a second view, the letters are declinable in principle, but lack the required condition of being in a syntactic construction.
rows.anchor: أنها معربة، بمعنى أنها صالحة للإعراب وإنما فات شرط وهو التركيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view treats the letters as paused forms, neither declinable nor indeclinable.
rows.anchor: أنها موقوفة لا معربة ولا مبنية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The letters may be sura names or remnants of divine names, with the remaining letters indicating the omitted parts.
rows.anchor: إنها بعض أسماء الله تعالى حذف بعضها، وبقي منها هذه الحروف دالة عليها وهو رأي ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they are sura names or abbreviated divine names, they have syntactic case: nominative as subject or predicate.
rows.anchor: فلها حينئذ محل إعراب، ويحتمل الرفع والجر/، فالرفع على أحد وجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative may come from an implied command to recite, or from deleting an oath particle that still governs the letters.
rows.anchor: والنصب على أحد وجهين أيضا: إما بإضمار فعل لائق تقديره: اقرؤوا: ألم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari objects that the oath analysis cannot explain the visibly genitive Quranic sequences without either two oaths on one object or an impossible conjunction.
rows.anchor: وقد رد الزمخشري هذا الوجه بما معناه: أن " القرآن " في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parse makes dhalika a second subject with al-kitab as its predicate, and the full clause the predicate of Alif Lam Mim, linked by the demonstrative.
rows.anchor: أن يكون مبتدأ ثانيا والكتاب خبره، والجملة خبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse makes Alif Lam Mim the subject and dhalika its predicate, with al-kitab as adjective, appositive, or explanatory substitute.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ و " ذلك " خبره و " الكتاب " صفة ل " ذلك " أو بدل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further parse makes Alif Lam Mim the subject and dhalika a second subject, with al-kitab modifying or explaining dhalika.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ ثان، و " الكتاب ": إما صفة له أو بدل منه أو عطف بيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La rayba fihi can predicate the second subject, with that clause then predicating the first.
rows.anchor: { لا ريب فيه } خبر عن المبتدأ الثاني، وهو وخبره خبر عن الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alif Lam Mim may instead complete an implied sentence meaning “these are Alif Lam Mim”; dhalika is then a subject with al-kitab as predicate or modifier, and la rayba predicates dhalika.
rows.anchor: خبر مبتدأ مضمر، تقديره: هذه ألم، فتكون جملة مستقلة بنفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-kitab may predicate dhalika and la rayba may be a second sentential predicate; the author accepts this despite a concern about multiple predicates, citing Taha 20 if tasʿa is a predicate.
rows.anchor: لكن الظاهر جوازه كقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted oath-particle genitive analysis is weak because such governance is peculiar to the divine name and cannot be extended to other nouns.
rows.anchor: والجر من وجه واحد وهو أنها مقسم بها، حذف حرف القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La is the genus-negating particle, patterned on inna; a singular indefinite noun is indeclinable on its accusative form because it implies the comprehensive min, as a poem makes explicit.
rows.anchor: سبب بنائه تضمنه معنى الحرف، وهو " من " الاستغراقية يدل على ذلك ظهورها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says la rajul has an inflected case ending with only tanwin omitted for lightness; the author rejects his poetic evidence, reading it as an omitted interrogative construction.
rows.anchor: وزعم الزجاج أن حركة " لا رجل " ونحوه حركة إعراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the noun is annexed or quasi-annexed rather than singular, la governs it in the accusative; la does not govern a definite noun.
rows.anchor: فإن لم يكن مفردا - وأعنى به المضاف والشبيه به- أعرب نصبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Apparent uses of genus-negating la with a definite name, including the prophetic saying about Quraysh and Khosrow, require interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقوله عليه السلام: " لا قريش بعد اليوم، إذا هلك كسرى فلا كسرى بعده "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The predicate of la rayba may be fihi, but since Banu Tamim often omit it, the preferable analysis supplies ka'in; the pause after rayb is then complete.
rows.anchor: تقديره: لا ريب كائن، ويكون الوقف على " ريب " حينئذ تاما

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh treats la with its noun as a nominative subject and says it does not govern the predicate.
rows.anchor: ومذهب سيبويه أنها واسمها في محل رفع بالابتداء ولا عمل لها في الخبر

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash instead makes the noun nominative while allowing la to govern its predicate.
rows.anchor: ومذهب الأخفش أن اسمها في محل رفع وهي عاملة في الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La can negate a genus or an individual, prohibit or supplicate by jussive verb, and sometimes function as an augmentative particle.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن " لا " لفظ مشترك بين النفي، وهي فيه على قسمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhalika consists of the demonstrative dha, a distance lām, and an address kāf; demonstratives have near, middle, and far degrees, though some grammarians count only two.
rows.anchor: واللام للبعد والكاف للخطاب وله ثلاث رتب: دنيا ولها المجرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basrans take dha as triliteral; they differ whether its middle and final radicals were ya's or waw then ya, while the author notes such derivation is only an exercise for an indeclinable form.
rows.anchor: الأول قول البصريين. ثم اختلفوا: هل عينه ولامه ياء فيكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The far demonstrative may honor the referent; other proposed reasons are its descent from heaven, its prior promise to the Prophet, or its decree in the Preserved Tablet. The author says the referent is mentally or physically present.
rows.anchor: وإنما جيء هنا بإشارة البعيد تعظيما للمشار إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kitab is originally a verbal noun, but can mean the written object; its root signifies gathering, as in an army unit and stitching a waterskin, and writing joins letters.
rows.anchor: والكتاب في الأصل مصدر، قال تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In established usage, writing means joining some letters of the alphabet to others.
rows.anchor: والكتابة عرفا: ضم بعض حروف الهجاء إلى بعض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rayb is doubt accompanied by suspicion, more specific than doubt in general; al-Zamakhshari describes its essence as agitation and unease, supported by a hadith about leaving what troubles you.
rows.anchor: والريب: الشك مع تهمة، قال:

rows.speaker: ابن الزبعرى
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zibara uses rayb in the sense of doubt, saying there is no rayb in the truth.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الزبعرى: 105 ليس في الحق يا أميمة ريب

rows.speaker: جميل بثينة
rows.claim: Jamil Buthayna uses rayb in the sense of suspicion or accusation between two people.
rows.anchor: قال جميل بثينة: 106 بثينة قالت: يا جميل أربتني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reported sense of rayb is need, illustrated by a line about satisfying every need of Tihama and Khaybar.
rows.anchor: قضينا من تهامة كل ريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudan may be a subject with fihi as preceding predicate if la has no predicate; if fihi predicates la, hudan has an omitted predicate inferred from it.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ وخبره " فيه " متقدما عليه إذا قلنا:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudan may predicate an omitted subject huwa, or be a second or third predicate of dhalika under alternative parses of al-kitab and la rayba.
rows.anchor: وأن يكون خبر مبتدأ مضمر تقديره هو هدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudan may be an accusative circumstantial phrase from dhalika or al-kitab, or from the pronoun in fihi; its nominal source can function emphatically as guidance itself, by an omitted noun, or as an active participle.
rows.anchor: وأن يكون منصوبا على الحال من " ذلك " أو من " الكتاب "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fihi may modify rayb or be governed by rayb, though the latter creates an extended la-noun; it is tenable if governed by what rayb implies rather than by rayb itself.
rows.anchor: صفة لريب فيتعلق بمحذوف، وأن يكون متعلقا بريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda is a verbal noun on faʿla; although only sara, baka, and huda were said to occur in this pattern, laqiyahu laqan supplies another example.
rows.anchor: مصدر على فعل، قالوا: ولم يجىء من هذا الوزن

rows.speaker: اللحياني
rows.claim: Al-Lihyani reports the masculine form huda as the only gender, while al-Farra reports that some Banu Asad feminize it.
rows.anchor: والهدى فيه لغتان: التذكير، ولم يذكر اللحياني غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fi primarily marks literal or figurative location, and can also indicate accompaniment, cause, equivalence to ʿala or bi, and comparison.
rows.anchor: معناها الظرفية حقيقة أو مجازا، نحو: زيد في الدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza reads the hāʾ in li-ahlihi imkuthu with kasra after a preceding yāʾ; Hafs similarly reads ʿāhada ʿalayhi Allāha and wa-mā ansānīhi follows the Hijazi form.
rows.anchor: غير الحجازيين، وقد قرأ حمزة

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: For fihi or minhu, the usual form when preceded by a consonant is shortened, but Ibn Kathir reads the hāʾ with full length; other forms are also attested.
rows.anchor: ويجوز الإشباع، وبه قرأ ابن كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lilmuttaqin attaches to hudan, though it may instead modify hudan with an implied predicate; best overall is to read the clauses independently and closely linked without conjunction.
rows.anchor: وإنما ترك العاطف لشدة الوصل

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says fronting fihi in the wine verse suggests worldly wine has gall, whereas fronting it here would wrongly suggest other scriptures contain doubt; the author says the explanation can be disputed.
rows.anchor: وكأن هذا الذي ذكره أبو القاسم الزمخشري بناء منه على أن التقديم يفيد الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic counterexample attributed in the preceding segment to Alqama describes worldly wine as not causing headache or heaviness, but the author says it is no valid rebuttal because the poet's description carries no authority.
rows.anchor: تشفي الصداع ولا يؤذيك صالبها ولا يخالطها في الرأس تدويم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best answer is that the Quran is not a proper object of doubt: fair-minded readers find decisive evidence, while negligent doubt is disregarded.
rows.anchor: أن المنفي كونه متعلقا للريب، بمعنى أن معه من الأدلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second answer restricts the negation to believers: there is no doubt in the Quran for them.
rows.anchor: والثاني: أنه مخصوص، والمعنى: لا ريب فيه عند المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third answer takes the declarative statement as a prohibition meaning do not doubt the Quran.
rows.anchor: والثالث: أنه خبر معناه النهي، أي لا ترتابوا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muttaqin derives from muttaqiyin; the first of two yāʾs is deleted under the weight of the kasra, then one of the adjacent sukūns is removed; the word is an iftiʿāl form from protection.
rows.anchor: وأصله متقيين بياءين، الأولى لام الكلمة والثانية علامة الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In iftiʿāl, an initial wāw or yāʾ changes to tāʾ when followed by the infix tāʾ, as in ittaʿada and ittasara; analogous hamza changes are rare.
rows.anchor: إلا أنه يطرد في الواو والياء إذا كانا فاءين ووقعت بعدهما تاء الافتعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iftiʿāl has twelve uses, including adoption, causation, reflexive action, selection, snatching, passive counterparts, reciprocal or intensive equivalents, equivalence to a simple verb, and replacing an unattested simple form.
rows.anchor: ولافتعل اثنا عشر معنى: الاتخاذ نحو: اتقى، والتسبب نحو:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wiqaya means intense protection and caution against harm, illustrated by a horse that protects its hoof; another view says its original sense is little speech.
rows.anchor: والوقاية: فرط الصيانة وشدة الاحتراس من المكروه، ومنه: فرس واق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The saying al-muttaqi muljam presents the God-fearing person as restrained; the cited poetry illustrates shielding or covering oneself with the hand.
rows.anchor: سقط النصيف ولم ترد إسقاطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second poem uses ittaqat in the sense of shielding oneself behind joined hands and forearm.
rows.anchor: فألقت قناعا دونه الشمس واتقت بأحسن موصولين كف ومعصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ya is the basic vocative particle, can be omitted, and marks lament and calls for help; a report says all Quranic vocatives use it.
rows.anchor: حرف نداء وهي أم الباب، وزعم بعضهم أنها اسم فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some unusually interpret the light-mīm reading of the phrase in 39:9 as hamza plus ya of address.
rows.anchor: أن قراءة { أمن هو قانت } [الزمر: 9] بتخفيف الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ya may serve as a mere attention marker before nominal or verbal clauses, as in the Quranic and poetic examples.
rows.anchor: وقد يراد بها مجرد التنبيه فيليها الجمل الاسمية والفعلية

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash analyzes ay as a relative pronoun, with an omitted subject and a relative clause meaning “those who are the people”; the author prefers direct address.
rows.anchor: وزعم الأخفش أنها هنا موصولة، وأن المرفوع بعدها خبر مبتدأ مضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ay is a nominative-built vocative in the accusative; its following adjective must be nominative, not accusative by attraction, contrary to al-Mazini.
rows.anchor: والمرفوع بعدها صفة لها يلزم رفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hāʾ is an obligatory added attention particle, usually fatḥa but sometimes ḍamma by assimilation to yāʾ; ʿAmir reads that way in some instances, supported by the written form.
rows.anchor: ويجوز ضمها إتباعا للياء، وقد قرأ عامر بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This ay may be modified only by a definite phrase, a relative pronoun containing the article, or a demonstrative; ay also has interrogative, conditional, relative, and other uses.
rows.anchor: هذه إلا بما فيه الألف واللام، أو بموصول هما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-nas is either an adjective of ay or the predicate of an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: صفة لأي، أو خبر مبتدأ محذوف حسبما تقدم من الخلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uʿbudu rabbakum is an initial imperative clause with no syntactic position.
rows.anchor: جملة أمرية لا محل لها لأنها ابتدائية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhi has three parses: accusative as an adjective to rabbakum, accusative by qatʿ, or nominative by qatʿ.
rows.anchor: فيه ثلاثة أوجه، أظهرها: نصبه على النعت لربكم. الثاني: نصبه على القطع.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhina is accusative by coordination with the object of khalaqakum; min qablikum is its relative clause and min marks the starting point.
rows.anchor: محله النصب لعطفه على المنصوب في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some object that min qablikum is incomplete as a relative clause; one answer supplies “who were from a time before your time.”
rows.anchor: واستشكل بعضهم وقوع " من قبلكم " صلة من حيث

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abu al-Baqa supplies the sense “those whom He created before your creation,” deleting creation and leaving its pronoun.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " التقدير: والذين خلقهم من قبل خلقكم

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Ali reads the mīm of min with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي: " والذين من قبلكم " بفتح الميم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the reading by inserting a second relative pronoun as emphasis between the first pronoun and its relative clause, analogously to repeated wording in poetry.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ووجهها على إشكالها أن يقال: أقحم الموصول الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A critic rejects insertion because an emphasized particle must repeat what it attaches to; an alternative makes the second relative clause predicate an omitted subject, though the author calls this strained.
rows.anchor: إلا أن بعضهم يرد هذا القول ويجعله فاسدا، من جهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalq can mean origination and creation, unique to God, or measuring and shaping, which is not exclusive to God.
rows.anchor: والخلق يقال باعتبارين، وأحدهما: الإبداع والاختراع، وهذه الصفة ينفرد بها الباري تعالى

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr uses khalq in the sense of measuring or shaping, which a person may do without successfully carrying it through.
rows.anchor: ولأنت تفري ما خلقت وبع

rows.speaker: الحجاج
rows.claim: Al-Hajjaj likewise uses khalq for planning or promising followed by carrying out the plan.
rows.anchor: وقال الحجاج: " ما خلقت إلا فريت ولا وعدت إلا وفيت "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects Abu Abd Allah al-Basri's denial that God may be called Creator on the ground that measuring and shaping would imply thought; Quranic usage names God Creator and creation also means origination.
rows.anchor: وقد غلط أبو عبد الله البصري في أنه لا يطلق اسم الخالق على الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites God as “the Creator, the Originator” and “Creator of everything” to refute the denial of the divine name al-Khaliq.
rows.anchor: وكأنه لم يعلم أن الخلق يكون عبارة عن الإنشاء والاختراع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laʿalla has a noun and predicate here; its use in divine speech has three reported analyses.
rows.anchor: لعل واسمها وخبرها، وإذا ورد ذلك في كلام الله تعالى

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: On its ordinary meaning of hope and inducement, laʿalla is relative to the addressees: they worship in hope of becoming God-fearing; Sibawayh applies this to Moses and Aaron.
rows.anchor: وكذا قال سيبويه في قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub, al-Tabari, and others take laʿalla causally, meaning “so that you may become God-fearing”; a poem uses it to mean “so that we may cease fighting.”
rows.anchor: وبه قال قطرب والطبري وغيرهما وأنشدوا

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: A third analysis takes laʿalla to mean acting in openness to attaining taqwa; al-Mahdawi and Abu al-Baqa favor attaching the clause semantically to the command to worship.
rows.anchor: وإليه مال المهدوي وأبو البقاء

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya sees laʿalla as attached to khalqakum: every child is born on the natural disposition and may therefore be expected to become God-fearing.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " يتجه تعلقها ب "

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawi objects that this cannot attach to creation, since those created for Hell were not created in order to become God-fearing.
rows.anchor: إلا أن المهدوي منع من ذلك، قال:

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari attaches laʿalla to khalqakum, says the plural includes earlier peoples by rhetorical dominance, and argues that taqwa is worship's ultimate aim rather than a repetition of worship.
rows.anchor: ولم يذكر الزمخشري غير تعلقها ب

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The Shaykh rejects al-Zamakhshari's appeal to matching the ends of the wording: “worship so you may worship” or “fear so you may fear” would be awkward and semantically defective.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وأما قوله: ليتجاوب طرفا النظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author attaches laʿalla to uʿbudu: worship is the commanded purpose, while the relative clause describes or praises the one worshipped rather than supplying a competing attachment.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر به صحته أن يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laʿalla has many dialect forms and can govern a genitive; on the correct view it does not put both nouns in the accusative, and an can enter its predicate by analogy with ʿasa.
rows.anchor: ولا تنصب الاسمين على الصحيح، وقد تدخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its basic meaning is expectation of desired things and apprehension regarding feared things, like ʿasa, though it can also convey question or cause.
rows.anchor: ولكن أصلها أن تكون للترجي والطمع في المحبوبات والإشفاق في المكروهات كعسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tattaqun derives from tawtaqiyun: wāw becomes tāʾ before the infix tāʾ and assimilates, then vowel and hiatus changes yield the current pattern taftaʿūn.
rows.anchor: وأصل تتقون: توتقيون لأنه من الوقاية، فأبدلت الواو تاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laʿallakum tattaqun cannot be a circumstantial clause because it is a request; tattaqun has an omitted object, such as shirk or the Fire.
rows.anchor: وهذه الجملة أعني " لعلكم تتقون " لا يجوز أن تكون حالا لأنها طلبية
